title: Trump Arrives in China for First-Ever Summit With Xi and Putin
summary: President Trump landed in southern China on Wednesday, November 18, after signing a trade deal and pledging increased defense cooperation with the Philippines. On Thursday, he was set to hold a summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen, China, on the sidelines of a meeting of Asia-Pacific countries. The meeting was described as historic because it would be the first ever formal meeting among the leaders of China, Russia, and the United States. There was no official agenda, but the topics were expected to include war and peace, Iran and Ukraine, trade, and nuclear weapons. Beijing said the meeting could have groundbreaking significance. In a rare show of respect, Xi personally greeted Trump at the airport. In his 14 years in power, China's leader had never personally greeted a foreign leader at the airport before, according to the report. The two leaders leaned into their promise to stabilize the relationship between the United States and China. Putin then joined hands with Trump ahead of their meeting on Thursday. Trump said he wants to talk about reducing nuclear weapons, a tough subject. China joined the United States, Russia, France, and Britain in the group of countries with nuclear weapons. For years after China's 1964 nuclear test, Beijing limited its stockpile to around 300 weapons. Today, Beijing tests nuclear-capable missiles, and its nuclear arsenal is the fastest growing in the world. The Pentagon says that by 2030, Beijing will have more than 1,000 nuclear warheads. That is still a fraction of the arsenals held by the United States and Russia. Xi has long refused to discuss arms control until China reaches parity, or an equal level, with the other powers. But talks involving all three countries have long been a priority for Trump. A professor at Hong Kong University, Li Cheng, said Beijing sees the meeting in the context of bringing the region's leaders together. He said China does not see it as a sequel to the 1945 Yalta summit, when Roosevelt, Churchill, and Stalin divided up Germany and Europe. For Putin, the meeting offered a chance to appear as a global statesman after meeting Xi.
why_it_matters: Decisions by the leaders of the United States, China, and Russia affect trade, wars, and nuclear weapons around the world, so their first-ever three-way meeting could shape how safe and stable the world feels for everyone.

background_read: A summit is a meeting where the leaders of countries talk face to face about big issues like trade, war and peace, and weapons.
The United States, Russia, China, France, and Britain are the countries known to have nuclear weapons, and leaders have long tried to agree on limits for them.
China kept its store of nuclear weapons small for many years, but it is now growing fast, which is why talks about arms control matter to all three countries.
Leaders also use summits to show respect and build trust, such as greeting a visitor in person at the airport.
